description: Five independent 20-game probes of the final checkpoint against a random opponent, seats rotated, 6 MCTS simulations (evaluate_against_random uses num_simulations // 2). Repeated because a single probe is not reproducible: the opponent RNG is seeded but MicroCivEnv.reset() is not, and training_civ6.py exposes no --seed flag, so each probe draws a fresh map. The first sample (score_rate 0.25) is an outlier against the other four.
interpretation: The model is worse than a random opponent at this budget: every probe's draw-aware score rate is below 0.5. The legacy win rate reported by evaluate_against_random (0.00-0.05) understates it badly, because a 50-75% draw rate is scored entirely as losses -- the same draw-blindness as the deployed promotion gate (docs/runbooks/promotion-gate.md). The draw rate here is close to the 73.5% measured independently in docs/evidence/hexcrystal_ab/, which supports that runbook's conclusion that the draw rate, not the threshold, is the upstream problem.
